To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stink bugs are more abundant in soybean than cotton, and they prefer early-maturing soybean varieties to late-maturing varieties.
stink bug abundance was much greater in soybeans than cotton and the early-maturing soybean was the first to be infested, followed by the later maturing soybean.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of integrated pest management (IPM) tactics for the management of stink bugs in cotton and soybean.
the seasonal abundance of stink bugs in soybean and cotton and the potential use of the two crops in an integrated pest management program.
the seasonal dynamics and relative abundance patterns of stink bug species in cotton and soybean.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N. viridula and A. hilare are the dominant pentatomid species found in cotton and soybean in the southern United States.

the stink bug population in the cotton-soybean system is a dynamic population, which is influenced by the phenology of the crops and the relative attractiveness of the crops to stink bugs. D. A. the dynamics and relative abundance (seasonal abundance) of stink bugs in the soybean–cotton ecosystem were influenced by crop phenology, plant maturity, and the availability of food resources (i.e., seeds and flowers).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
early-maturing group V cultivars should be planted in a trap crop system with late-maturing group VIs, and that the trap crops should be planted in the first week of June.
the most abundant pentatomids in both crops for 3 yr were N. viridula, A. hilare, and E. servus.
early-maturing soybean varieties can attract and retain stink bugs until the later-maturing soybean variety is at the appropriate stage to attract the insects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
soybean can serve as an effective trap crop for stink bug control in cotton.

the dynamics and relative abundance (i.e., the numbers of each species) of stink bugs in a cotton–soybean ecosystem are similar to those of stink bugs that occur in a monoculture of either cotton or soybean.
soybean is a more important crop than cotton in terms of the number of stink bugs found on each crop.
